title: Authentication System
description: Build a complete authentication system with JWT access tokens, refresh tokens, password hashing, and role-based access control.

steps.title: Implement password hashing with salt
steps.description: Write a `hashPassword` function that takes a plaintext password, generates a random salt using crypto random bytes, and returns a combined salt+hash string (e.g. base64 encoded). Use SHA-256 HMAC. Print the resulting hash to verify it works.
hints: Generate 16 random bytes for the salt using crypto.randomBytes or os.urandom
Hash the password concatenated with the salt using SHA-256
Return salt and hash concatenated with a delimiter like ':' so they can be split later

verification.successMessage: Password hashing with random salt produces a unique hash each time!
verification.failureMessage: Your hashPassword function should print the salt and hash. Make sure you use a random salt per call.

steps.title: Create JWT token generation
steps.description: Implement a `generateToken` function that creates a JWT using the HS256 algorithm. Build the header and payload manually, base64url encode them, compute the HMAC-SHA256 signature, and produce the full token string (header.payload.signature). Print the generated token.
hints: Payload: include 'sub' (user id), 'iat' (issued at), 'exp' (expiration) as epoch seconds
Signature: HMAC-SHA256 of base64url(header) + '.' + base64url(payload) using your secret key

verification.successMessage: JWT token with correct header.payload.signature format is generated!
verification.failureMessage: Your token must have exactly 3 dot-separated segments. Print the full token to the console.

steps.title: Implement access token verification
steps.description: Write a `verifyToken` function that takes a JWT string and a secret, splits it into parts, recomputes the HMAC signature, and compares it to the provided signature. Decode and print the payload. Return null if the token is invalid or expired.
hints: Split on '.' to get header, payload, and signature segments
Recompute the HMAC-SHA256 signature and compare using constant-time comparison
Check the 'exp' claim against current time — if expired, print 'Token expired' and return null

verification.successMessage: Token verification correctly decodes the payload and detects invalid tokens!
verification.failureMessage: Print the decoded payload from a valid token and show 'invalid token' for a tampered one.

steps.title: Add refresh token rotation
steps.description: Implement a refresh token system with rotation. Create a `generateRefreshToken` function that produces a cryptographically random token, stores it in an in-memory store mapped to a user ID, and returns it. Write a `rotateRefreshToken` that invalidates the old token and issues a new one. Print the refresh token and rotation result.
hints: Use crypto.randomBytes(32) and convert to hex for the refresh token value
Store tokens in a Map or object: refreshTokenStore.set(token, { userId, createdAt })
On rotation, delete the old token from the store before inserting the new one

verification.successMessage: Refresh token rotation works — old token is invalidated and a new one is issued!
verification.failureMessage: Print the generated refresh token and confirm rotation. Show that the old token is no longer valid.

steps.title: Implement role-based access control
steps.description: Write a `checkPermission` function that takes a user object (with a `role` property) and an array of allowed roles, and returns true if the user's role is in the allowed list. Then build a `requireRole` middleware-style function that wraps another function and checks permissions before executing. Print pass/fail results for admin, user, and guest roles.
hints: requireRole returns a wrapper function that checks permission first, then calls the original function if allowed
Test with at least three roles: 'admin', 'user', and 'guest' against a route requiring 'admin' access

verification.successMessage: Role-based access control correctly grants or denies access based on user role!
verification.failureMessage: Show that an admin is granted access, a guest is denied, and print the permission check results.

steps.title: Build a login flow
steps.description: Combine all components into a `login` function. It takes a username and password, looks up the user, verifies the password hash, generates both an access token and a refresh token, and returns them. Write a `refreshAccessToken` function that uses a valid refresh token to issue a new access token. Print both tokens from a successful login and a failed login attempt.
hints: Store user objects with hashed passwords and roles — look up by username
On successful login: call generateAccessToken and generateRefreshToken, print both
On failed login (wrong password or unknown user): print 'Invalid credentials' and return null

verification.successMessage: Complete login flow works — valid credentials return both tokens, invalid ones are rejected!
verification.failureMessage: Print both tokens on successful login and show an error message for invalid credentials.
